request.text: Welcome to the running Living Town. The original coastal center, eighty-one new buildings, and a wooded natural reserve share one playable world. This opening is a labelled camera inspection of the actual game.

Streets follow changing ground. Buildings turn with their frontages, and planted courts break up the blocks. Beyond the town, paths lead into woodland, mountain slopes, and visitor facilities. We will walk between these places as Aria.

We choose the existing resident Aria. Her upper home remains above the cafe. Her name, job, money, needs, and saved identity belong to the same life simulation. The refined character is a real articulated three-dimensional model.

Her five needs stay visible in the compact resident card. Time and speed controls remain at the top. We can expand the activity history and daily wishes when needed, then close them to keep the town in view.

Aria takes the actual stairs downstairs. Walls and furnishings constrain her route. Door openings and clear landings matter. Each floor has its own spatial address, so an upstairs resident cannot interact through a ceiling.

At the cafe table, we open the real action menu and choose a meal. Aria approaches the furnishing and uses it. The recording checks an actual completion event and a measurable need change, rather than mistaking a closed menu for success.

The counter also offers the existing permitted actions. We observe the result, then leave through the cafe entrance. Interior cutaways expose the active floor while neighboring roofs stay in place. The original access rules continue to apply.

Outside, Aria keeps normal depth against buildings and vegetation. When geometry blocks the controlled resident, an amber mesh silhouette preserves her location. The main character stays shaded by the scene, and ordinary residents keep their own depth.

Now we walk from the original center into a new district. A screen click requests the actual entrance. The camera returns to Aria so the journey remains visible. Every step comes from the existing movement system.

This is a connected extension of the running town. Roads, approaches, building pads, and entrances share an authored terrain profile. The new building has actual rooms and furniture, with reachable interaction positions beside its fixtures.

Inside the new venue, we use a physical furnishing through the same action menu. The recorded outcome comes from the simulation. Selected new fixtures reuse compatible existing actions, while shelves, flowers, and decorative objects remain visual detail.

Where this venue has another floor, we take its genuine stairs and return. The model exposes the selected level. Floor slabs and door gaps agree with the authored spatial profile, preserving room boundaries and usable circulation.

Our next journey reaches the reserve visitor facilities. Woodland surrounds the town rather than ending at a flat edge. The route follows connected paths and terraces, with building thresholds attached to the same graded landscape.

At the public bathhouse, we enter through the actual door and use a hygiene fixture. Shower, basin, and toilet areas have separate compartments and clear approaches. The service applies the existing need rules and produces a real completion.

The camping area contains furnished trailers. Aria walks to one and enters through its actual doorway. Compact circulation, storage, kitchen fittings, sleeping space, and the bathroom make this a small interior rather than an empty exterior shell.

We use a real trailer fixture through the normal menu, then return outside. These close views show furniture grouping, material scale, and the character pose. Detailed models support the activity; they do not grant movement through a wall.

The return to town uses the same real walking controls. Aria leaves the camping area and follows the connected paths back through the expanded districts. Her position changes one legal step at a time; the camera follows the resident throughout.

The cafe is our original point of departure. Reaching its door again closes a complete trip from the old center to the new town and reserve, and back. Doorways, room changes, and furnishing actions all use the existing life simulation.

We now pause for labelled architectural inspection. These camera cuts show the ravine bridge, the mountain stone stairs, and their surrounding vegetation. They do not imply that Aria has crossed every structure shown by the camera.

The pond has graded banks and planted edges. Trees, understory, flowers, and horticultural groupings create different scales of enclosure. Shared botanical meshes are batched by area in the running game, while stable identities remain in the asset catalog.

We return to actual resident life, save with F five, continue, and load with F eight. The recording verifies the saved tick and spatial address. A changed or incompatible town profile is rejected instead of silently moving the resident.

After loading, we enable existing free will. Needs, jobs, access, and circumstances guide the next decisions. The renderer follows those decisions. It does not create another simulation, and the recording does not force a desired social response.
We have followed real walking, rooms, services, stairs, and saved life. Separate building reports cover the wider town and distinguish camera inspections.
Editable Blender sources, portable models, the playable town, and recorded evidence travel together. This final overview still shows the running game.
